name: Hand and Foot
tagline: Canasta's big family cousin: play out your hand, pick up your foot, build piles with your partner.
rulesSummary: Four play as two partnerships, partners across; six as two teams of three, alternate seats; two, three or five each play for themselves. One more deck than players, jokers in. Everyone gets a 13-card hand and a 13-card foot, kept face down until the hand is played out.
Each turn: draw 2 from the stock, or take the top 7 of the discard pile by melding its top card with two of the same rank from your hand. Then meld and discard.
Melds are 3 to 7 cards of one rank (4s to aces). 2s and jokers are wild: one in a meld of up to five cards, two in six or seven. Three or more wilds can make a wild meld.
Seven cards make a pile: clean (no wilds) 500, dirty 300, wild 1500. Red 3s are laid out at once for 100; black 3s can't be melded and block the pile.
Your side's first meld must be worth 50, then 90, 120 and 150 in rounds two to four.
Play out your hand and you pick up your foot. To go out your side needs 2 clean, 2 dirty and 1 wild pile, with every partner in their foot. Going out is worth 100.
Melded cards score their value; cards left in hand or foot count against you. Highest total after four rounds wins.
